Senses.PreferredTarget: not be a companion to the myriad things
AlternateTargets: the one who is not a companion to the myriad things
SearchAliases: not companion to the ten thousand things
who is not companion to all things
not partner with the myriad things
Senses.Explanation: Layman Pang’s fixed public question—who is not a companion of the ten thousand things?—is repeatedly raised afresh and answered in later records. Literally, not to be or become a companion to the myriad things. The expression is overwhelmingly recorded in the question, 'Who is the one who is not a companion to the myriad things?' The Compendium of the Five Lamps records Layman Pang asking it first of Shitou Xiqian, who covers Pang's mouth, and later of Mazu Daoyi, who answers, 'When you swallow the West River in one mouthful, I will tell you.' Later masters quote Pang's question as a named public case, ask it afresh, and give their own answers. Letan Huaicheng answers 'Guanyin' (觀世音菩薩). Caoshan Benji answers, 'Where did all those many people in Hongzhou city go?' (汝道洪州城裏如許多人甚麼處去). Asked directly, 'Ultimately, what is not being a companion to the myriad things?' (畢竟如何是不與萬法為侶), Yinyuan Longqi answers, 'Passing through a hundred flowers, not one leaf clings to the body' (百花叢裏過，一葉不沾身). Xingkong Zhen answers another fresh raising with 'standing openly revealed' (堂堂獨露). Yuanwu Keqin's instruction says that the ancients called someone 'the person who is not a companion to the myriad things' (古人謂之不與萬法為侶底人). Zhang Jun's preface to Yuanwu's record says that whenever Yuanwu raised this public case, it was already dragging through mud and water and falling into the second meaning. The entry preserves the fixed wording, its named origin, and the answers that the record attaches to it.
Senses.Note: The exact phrase has 446 matches in 153 files. The person-question form has 139 matches in 73 files, while the longer nominal form ending in 'the one who' has 269 matches in 117. Three passages in three files directly ask, 'What is not being a companion to the myriad things?' One text explicitly calls it the public case of not being companion to the myriad things, and one instruction uses the naming formula 'the ancients called him the person who is not a companion to the myriad things.' The distribution supports one corpus-wide fixed expression rather than a meaning restricted to Layman Pang, Shitou, or Mazu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 唐貞元初謁石頭。乃問。不與萬法為侶者是甚麼人。頭以手掩其口。豁然有省。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Pang Yun, in (五燈會元) (Compendium of the Five Lamps), asks Shitou who is not a companion to the myriad things.

Occurrences.Kwic: 後參馬祖。問曰。不與萬法為侶者是甚麼人。祖曰。待汝一口吸盡西江水。即向汝道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Pang Yun, in (五燈會元) (Compendium of the Five Lamps), asks Mazu the fixed question; Mazu gives the West River answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云不與萬法為侶者豈不是出塵勞耶心不知心眼不見眼既絕對待
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Foyan Qingyuan, in (古尊宿語錄) (Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters), asks whether the one not companion to myriad things is not beyond dusty toil.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若有問山僧：『不與萬法為侶是什麼人？』便向他道：『堂堂獨露。』他若擬議，連棒打出。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Xingkong Zhen, in (性空臻禪師語錄) (Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xingkong Zhen), poses the question himself and gives 'standing openly revealed' as his answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 每舉到不與萬法為侶公案。已是拕泥帶水。落第二義。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (圓悟佛果禪師語錄). The official Zhang Jun authors the later commentary about repeatedly raising the case.

ActorAttribution.ReviewedBy: Codex lane-C second independent semantic repair
ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The passage is Zhang Jun’s signed preface (張浚序); in his own first-person assessment he says that every raising of Pang’s case already drags through mud and water.

Occurrences.Kwic: 古人謂之不與萬法為侶底人，亦號如來正徧知覺。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu Keqin, in (佛果克勤禪師心要) (Essentials of Chan Master Foguo Keqin), gives the ancient naming formula for this person.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問不與萬法為侶者是什麼人。師曰。觀世音菩薩。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), section on Letan Huaicheng, Letan answers the fixed person-question with 'Guanyin.' Letan Huaicheng is source-attested; roster reconciliation is deferred.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問。不與萬法為侶者是甚麼人。師曰。汝道洪州城裏如許多人甚麼處去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Caoshan Yuanzheng of Fuzhou (撫州曹山元證禪師語錄), Caoshan Benji answers the fixed person-question, 'Where did all those many people in Hongzhou city go?'

Occurrences.Kwic: 少頃問云：「畢竟如何是不與萬法為侶？」師云：「百花叢裏過，一葉不沾身。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan (隱元禪師語錄), Yinyuan Longqi answers the direct question 'Ultimately, what is not being a companion to the myriad things?' with 'Passing through a hundred flowers, not one leaf clings to the body.'
